piece_title: The Morrowind screens, round 7 — the container's ink, its numbers, and the header now printed across the first row

critic.note: The brief handed me the builder's status file as the work list, so I read it before measuring — CRITIC-DOCTRINE §8 asks for the reverse order and this is recorded rather than hidden. Every number below was re-derived on my own arms; where a figure of the builder's is quoted un-re-derived it is labelled as such.

build.prior_pin: b0a9f7168c0b49b0c56c8de0245b8d49a85a28ec (round 6) / 8cde4128 (my BEFORE arm, which carries round 6's game/src/ui)
build.note: `git diff a2ef1e5c HEAD -- game/src/ui/` is empty at the time of judging, so the geometry I measured is the geometry shipped. Verified this run.

headline: Every number the round published reproduces on my own arms, and the round really did buy its density with ink rather than with a smaller denominator — but it also moved the side headers down onto the first list row, and both of the round's own instruments and the corpus's legibility pass call that clean. Two text elements now overlap by 190x20 units at 1920x1080, where round 6's overlap was 182x12 and the glyphs did not touch. RI-UIX06 FD4's hard fail is 'any clipping, overlap or overflow at 1920x1080', so the container's 0.1685 does not count under S58 either. C7 is still violated and now has nowhere to go: 25 of 45 records truncate at rest and 22 bound controls reach none of the missing text, which is exactly what S65's guard (b) fails.

is_it_the_denominator_trick_in_a_new_coa.the_question_the_brief_asked: The box got SMALLER (460 -> 452) and D2 rose 0.1459 -> 0.1685. S56/S58's usual mechanism is a falling denominator, so the shape deserved scepticism.
is_it_the_denominator_trick_in_a_new_coa.arithmetic_from_the_two_manifests: r6 panel 480x460 = 220,800 px at 0.1459 = 32,215 ink px. r7 panel 480x452 = 216,960 px at 0.1685 = 36,558 ink px. A pure denominator shrink would have moved 0.1459 -> 0.1485. The observed move is +0.0226, of which the denominator explains +0.0026 (11%) and +4,343 NEW INK PIXELS (+13.5%) explain +0.0200 (89%).
is_it_the_denominator_trick_in_a_new_coa.ruling: NOT the denominator trick. The ink is real: the depiction plate grew and two more description lines are drawn. The builder's account of where the units came from is confirmed in its arithmetic.
is_it_the_denominator_trick_in_a_new_coa.s57_a_no_element_type_disappeared: Element count 33 both rounds; kinds byte-identical between my r7 manifest and the r6 critic's HEAD manifest — `list_row: 7`, `item_icon: 8`, `panel_header: 3`, `detail_panel: 1`, `hint: 1`, `divider: 1`, `scroll_extent: 1`. Nothing was traded away for the density.
is_it_the_denominator_trick_in_a_new_coa.s57_b_reachability_driven_not_argued: 44 of 44 carried records are selectable through 8 drawn rows with real ArrowDown presses (t4-r7-critic-drive.mjs G7). The smaller box hides nothing.

r1_reads_the_draw_now_and_i_drove_it_on_.and_the_arm_can_disagree: My hostile probe is numeric rather than nominal, because R1b probes the NAME column and the claim under test is about NUMBERS. A record with weight 987654.5 and gold 987654321, laid out by the shipped drawContainer(): the gold column came back `987654321 -> 98765…`, `truncated: true`. So the reader fires on a number, and — see below — the headline it certifies is narrower than the headline says.

the_headline_that_is_false_as_written.claim: b9b48766's headline and the builder's own caveat: 'no numeric column CAN truncate again' / 'they cannot truncate' because the columns are sized to the widest value in both lists.
the_headline_that_is_false_as_written.measured: They can. At gold 987654321 the gold column truncates and the name column is squeezed to 52.81 units. The column pitch has a ceiling; the guarantee is a property of today's DATA (max gold in carried.json is 400), not of the layout.
the_headline_that_is_false_as_written.why_it_matters_and_why_it_is_not_the_gap: Round 6's defect was a numeric truncation arriving from a layout change. The protection against a recurrence is data-dependent, so the next screen that shows a five-figure price re-opens it. It is not the gap because no shipped record triggers it — filed as a secondary observation and against the corpus hole the r6 critic already named.

clause_2_is_worse_than_the_builder_repor.measured_on_the_fixture_the_remedy_NAMES: 5 of 7 rows — 'Black-water draught -> Black-wat…', 'Bog-iron maul -> Bog-iron m…' (both sides), 'Boiled hide jack -> Boiled hide…', 'Rootweave cowl -> Rootweav…'. The remedy asks for at most 1. The builder's 2 was honest and was measured on a 4-row default-state fixture; its own offline arithmetic already predicted 5 over-long names, so this is a sampling gap, not a false claim.
clause_2_is_worse_than_the_builder_repor.and_the_builders_ruling_against_widening: Growing 480 -> 520 divides D2 by 1.083 to about 0.1555, margin 0.0055 inside the published band 0.0159 -> unresolved -> fails closed. Trading a resolved pass for an unresolved one to satisfy a prose clause is round 6's mistake with the sign flipped, and refusing it was right. The named cheapest partial (gutter 24 -> 12, +6 units per side at no cost in panel area) is correct arithmetic and is not the gap either — it clears 2 of 5.

the_defect_the_round_could_not_see_and_n.what: The container's side headers are now drawn ON the first list row. `container.mine.head` ('Carried') and `container.theirs.head` ('Reed Creel') each intersect the first row of their own list by 190x20 units at 1920x1080. Round 6's same rects intersected by 182x12 and the GLYPHS did not touch; at r7 they do — 'Carried' is broken by the Bark token's icon and 'Reed Creel' is printed through 'Bog-iron m…'.
the_defect_the_round_could_not_see_and_n.how_it_was_found: By looking at a 2x crop of the panel, which is the one thing no number in this round did. Then made geometric: `tools/ui/t4-r7-critic-headers.mjs` enumerates every text-bearing element's declared rect and reports partial intersections. Two arms, each run through ITS OWN worktree's copy of the tool (HAZARDS 22): AFTER at a2ef1e5c reports 2 collisions at 190x20; BEFORE at 8cde4128 (which carries round 6's `game/src/ui`) reports the same two pairs at 182x12.
the_defect_the_round_could_not_see_and_n.why_no_instrument_caught_it: `tools/ui/t4-r5-legibility.mjs` — the pass S58 exists to require — reports the container `overflow=0 truncation=0 overlap=0 -> clean` at BOTH 1920x1080 and 1280x720, run at the delivered commit through the delivered worktree's own copy. Its OVERLAP metric is round 4's column-run test INSIDE one row band, so two DIFFERENT elements landing on each other is outside what it can see. This is the project's own sentence arriving again: a statistic can fail a build and can never pass one.
the_defect_the_round_could_not_see_and_n.attribution_stated_without_a_narrated_me: I did not ablate the single constant. What I have is: the two arms, the two crops, and the builder's own statement that it took 16 units out of the inner top gap (density 0.0592) and 18 out of the list/band gap to pay for the depiction and the extra description lines. The collision deepened across exactly that change; I am reporting the correlation and the arms, not a cause I did not isolate (S63).
the_defect_the_round_could_not_see_and_n.what_it_costs_the_round: RI-UIX06 FD4's hard-fail clause is literally 'any [clipping, overlap or overflow] at 1920x1080' — so the FIDELITY side caps at 2. And S58 makes DN4 'necessary and not sufficient: a density figure counts only when accompanied by a legibility pass — no glyph overlapping another glyph'. The container's 0.1685 is a real number and it does not count while two glyph-bearing elements sit on top of each other.

S65_1_applied_C7_has_no_route.the_ruling_i_was_told_to_apply: C7 is SCOPED, not weakened: the full description must be reachable without leaving the screen, in ONE input; guard (b) — no ellipsis without a route; and if no expansion affordance exists yet, C7 FAILS.
S65_1_applied_C7_has_no_route.measured: With a record selected whose description the band cannot hold (needs 5 lines, shows 4), I pressed every bound desktop control — KeyE, Enter, KeyF, KeyV, KeyR, Space, KeyX, Digit1, Digit2, Tab, KeyG, Digit3, Digit4, KeyC, KeyZ, KeyT, ShiftLeft, KeyW, KeyS, and three unbound candidates (KeyQ, KeyH, KeyI) — 22 in all, each from a freshly reopened container, re-reading `description_lines_shown` and every text element on screen after each press. NONE increased the lines shown and NONE put the remainder of the string anywhere on screen.
S65_1_applied_C7_has_no_route.the_population_driven_rather_than_comput: 20 of 45 records are complete at rest; 25 are not. Needed-line histogram {1:2, 3:1, 4:17, 5:23, 6:2}. This reproduces the builder's headline figure of 20 of 45 — which it derived offline through the game's own wrap() — from a driven run with the record identity asserted, and it is the number I score against.
S65_1_applied_C7_has_no_route.verdict: C7 FAILS, and it fails on the ruling's own terms rather than on the old ones. RI-UIX03 M-C3 requires all four of C6/C7/C8/C9, so M-C3 fails a third round running.
S65_1_applied_C7_has_no_route.what_would_pass_it: One input on the container screen that puts the whole string in front of the player — S65 names the Morrowind press-to-read expansion — driven through the shipped handler under §1.2b, with the resting band keeping DN5's depiction and DN4's floor.

S65_2_the_band_re_derived_by_a_second_im.why: Every D2 in this thread — round 5's, 6's, 7's, and the band that decides the container — comes out of one function. An instrument nobody has re-implemented is an instrument nobody has checked. `tools/ui/t4-r7-critic-d2.mjs` implements RI-UIX09 method 4 from the item's own words on top of `tools/lib/colour.mjs`, and reads no number from the tool it checks.
S65_2_the_band_re_derived_by_a_second_im.reproduction: container 0.1681 (tool: 0.1685); container_no_name 0.1599 (0.1600). Two independent implementations agree to 0.0004 on the screen under judgement.
S65_2_the_band_re_derived_by_a_second_im.band_perturb_CONFIRMED_INDEPENDENTLY: 0.0000 on container, container_no_name and levelup — 6 seeds, +-1 LSB on 0.06% of the panel's pixels, D2 recomputed end to end including the modal re-derivation. The builder's central job-3 finding is true out of other code: the dither does not move D2, and averaging or denoising buys nothing.
S65_2_the_band_re_derived_by_a_second_im.band_mode_confirmed_by_the_bucket_counts: On the container the modal bucket holds 88,368 pixels against a runner-up of 27,125 (3.3x). It cannot be promoted by a perturbation of that size — which is the builder's `rival_buckets_considered = 0`, arrived at differently.

AND_A_THING_THE_BUILDER_DID_NOT_FIND.what: On LEVEL-UP the two implementations disagree across DN4's floor. The shipped `d2()` bins colour into 15-bit buckets (`>>3` per channel), picks the modal BIN and averages the true colours inside it, giving reference [220,217,204] and D2 0.1494. Exact-colour modal picking gives [223,223,216] and D2 0.1625. The level-up panel's modal bucket holds 7,673 pixels against a runner-up of 5,525 (1.39x), so the reference is genuinely contested there in a way the container's is not.
AND_A_THING_THE_BUILDER_DID_NOT_FIND.why_it_matters: The hard fail that caps this piece at 2 is a level-up reading that flips from 0.1494 (fail) to 0.1625 (pass) on a defensible change of reference-derivation convention that the reference item does not specify. That is S61's instability with a new face — not noise in the pixels, but a convention the row never pinned.
AND_A_THING_THE_BUILDER_DID_NOT_FIND.what_i_did_with_it: NOTHING IN THE PASSING DIRECTION. I scored level-up FAIL on the shipped instrument, fail-closed, exactly as it stands. A critic that rescues a build with an instrument it wrote this evening has graded its own work (§1.3 guard 2). It is filed as a corpus defect for RI-UIX09's owner, with the fix S65(2) already names: pin the reference to the declared ground colour from `getUIState().materials`, and specify the derivation in the item so two honest implementations cannot land on opposite sides of a hard floor.

S65_2_the_band_re_derived_by_a_second_im.how_i_scored_the_container: Against the band the build published (0.0159), per the brief. My own reference-shift arm gives the container 0.0051 over shifts up to 1.58 dE00, so the container's margin of 0.0185 clears both bands and the pass does not depend on which one you use.

bifurcation.note: === VIS DECLARATION === PASS 1, JUDGEMENT SIDE: ART_DIRECTION. PROPERTIES: RI-UIX09 populated density and object iconography, RI-UIX06 P09. PERMITTED: REF-A12b Morrowind interface plates, RI-VIS05 §H. FORBIDDEN: every modern AAA screenshot. === PASS 2, JUDGEMENT SIDE: FIDELITY. PROPERTIES: F18 layout integrity, M-F18.1/2/3. PERMITTED: our own captures at 1920x1080 and 1280x720. FORBIDDEN: every Morrowind plate. Both declared before any reference was cited. The defect I promote is geometric — two declared rects intersecting, with the glyph collision visible in a same-crop-box two-arm pair — and is judged on the fidelity side only. CC-7 was NOT used: nothing low-fidelity is excused here as art direction.

`git diff a2ef1e5c 378c9352 -- game/src/ui/` is empty, as the builder states — verified this run — so the drive report at 378c9352 and the measure at a2ef1e5c describe the same geometry.

The container's own drive fixture and the measure tool's fixture differ (4 rows against 7). Two instruments measuring 'the container' on different fixtures is how a round reports 2 truncated names where the shipped screen shows 5; the T4 instruments should share one fixture definition.

corpus_defects_filed.what: D2 is 'the modal colour of the panel rect', which does not say how the mode is taken. The shipped `d2()` bins colour into 15-bit buckets (`>>3` per channel), picks the modal BIN and averages the true colours inside it. An exact-colour modal pick is an equally faithful reading of the same sentence. On the container the two agree to 0.0004 (0.1685 vs 0.1681). On LEVEL-UP they disagree across the hard floor: reference [220,217,204] -> D2 0.1494 (fail) versus [223,223,216] -> D2 0.1625 (pass), because level-up's modal bucket holds 7,673 pixels against a runner-up of 5,525.
corpus_defects_filed.why_it_matters: The hard fail that caps this piece at 2 — and capped round 6 at 2 — is a reading that flips sides on a convention the reference item never wrote down. This is the same family as S61 (unstable) but the instability is in the DEFINITION rather than in the pixels, and no perturbation test can find it.

arbitration_questions.question: S58 requires a legibility pass alongside DN4 — 'no glyph overlapping another glyph'. The instrument built to run it (`tools/ui/t4-r5-legibility.mjs`) reports the container clean while two headers are drawn through two rows, because its OVERLAP metric is a column-run test inside a single row band. Does an S58 pass that cannot see element-versus-element collision satisfy S58?
arbitration_questions.my_working_answer_which_the_owner_may_re: No. I scored the piece as if it does not, and I have specified the missing check (pairwise text-rect intersection, 90 lines, already written) inside the remedy rather than landing it in the tool myself, because a critic that loosens or extends the instrument it is grading with is in the same conflict that kept the r6 critic off `t4-r4-critic-overlap.mjs`. The next builder or the orchestrator may land it directly; it bears on no score here, because I failed the piece on the geometry and the crops, not on the tool.

arbitration_questions.question: S65(2) says the fix for the moving band is to pin the reference to `getUIState().materials`. My independent implementation shows a sharper version of the same problem: RI-UIX09 does not say HOW the modal colour is taken, and on level-up two faithful readings of the item's sentence land at 0.1494 (fail) and 0.1625 (pass). Should DN4's hard fail be allowed to fire while the reference derivation is unspecified?
arbitration_questions.not_ruled_by_me: I scored level-up FAIL on the shipped instrument exactly as it stands, because rescuing a build with an instrument I wrote this evening is the one thing §1.3 forbids. Escalation ladder: step 1 (zoom — the 2x and 3x crops) is what found the gap; step 2 (change the sample — the 45-record scan and the shipped 7-row fixture instead of the 4-row one) is what found clause 2's real number; step 3 (stress — the 987654321-gold probe and the 45-row container walk) is what falsified the 'cannot truncate' headline.

notes: The builder ruled against itself in three places and every one of those rulings holds up: K0 really is its instrument and not the game (my arm drives the same screen green); the ancestry check really does clear the recovered arm; and its refusal to widen the panel for clause 2 really would have traded a resolved pass for an unresolved one. It also volunteered the caveat that the columns re-pitch when a wider price appears — which is the thread I pulled to falsify its own headline.

The thing worth taking out of this round beyond the screen: EVERY NUMBER IN IT WAS RIGHT AND THE SCREEN GOT WORSE ANYWAY. Seven density figures reproduced to four decimals, an ink budget decomposed to the pixel, a band re-derived four ways, three checks repaired from 'could not fail' to 'can fail' — and the defect that caps the piece was found by cropping the picture at 2x and reading it. The owner's directive from 2026-08-14 is the whole lesson: static inspection is not evidence, and a screen full of green instruments is not a screen anybody looked at.

I extended nothing in the corpus. I wrote one instrument (`t4-r7-critic-headers.mjs`) and it is used only to fail the piece; the row it enforces (S58's 'no glyph overlapping another glyph', RI-UIX06 FD4's 'any overlap at 1920x1080') was already written and already binding.
